findings.title: Favor's side-turn and harm's touch
findings.claim: With bestowed well-being, the human turns away and gives the gift distance; when harm touches, the focus names despair. Wider parallels make these a condition-shaped posture while leaving other responses to harm visible.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries bestowal in أَنْعَمْنَا, then turns the body through أَعْرَضَ and نَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ; مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ meets the predicate يَـُٔوسًا. The 17:67 rescue scene repeats turning after safety, 41:49 repeats harm-touch followed by despair, and 10:12 places calls during harm before forgetfulness after relief. The near-verbatim 41:51 parallel answers harm with broad prayer, while 21:83 answers harm-touch with appeal; 23:3 also shows turning away serving attentive refusal. These contacts make the bodily distance and despair one conditional configuration rather than an invariant law.
findings.reader_payoff: The side, distance, touch, and hope terms read as connected changes in orientation, while the wider counter-scenes keep despair and withdrawal from becoming the only possible responses.
findings.containment: The focus's own outcomes remain intact. 41:51 and 21:83 preserve prayer under harm, and 23:3 preserves constructive turning away. The connection rows supply target Arabic but not target morphology, so their wider relations remain contextual rather than asserted lexical joins.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run publication supplies the anchored focus synthesis. Wider connection rows provide exact Arabic and distinct counter-responses, but target morphology is not supplied.
